text:
maya: Quick brain-dump — thinking about a proportional/priority sampling layer that allocates a sampling budget per route based on recent RPS and tenant priority. Goal: avoid starving low-RPS but high-SLA customers while throttling noisy public routes. High level: short window counters -> weights -> per-route reservoir. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

liam: SGTM. curious how you see head vs tail sampling mixing in — we still want tail for error-heavy traces, right?

ana: I think hybrid is key. Head sampling to keep collector CPU down and still capture fast-fail errors, tail sampling for slow or high-resource traces we flagged (errors, high-latency, anomalous token counts).

maya: yes. proposal: budget B per minute per shard. For each route r compute weight w_r = alpha * recent_rps_r + beta * priority_score_r. Then sample_prob_r = clamp(k * w_r / sum_w, min_p, max_p). Default fallback: if trace contains error or spans > N, mark for tail-sampling override.

raj: Implementation note — the collector can't keep precise counters for every route/tenant. We should use approximate counters (CMS or decaying reservoir) and an eviction policy. Also keep config to cap per-tenant absolute tokens to avoid bill surprises.

telemetry-bot: snippet saved to gist: https://internal.gists/reproportional-sampler (acl: eng-platform)

liam: can you paste the sampler config we talked about? small example would help ops and console wiring.

maya: sure — config sketch:```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
exporters:
  redwood-exporter:
processors:
  proportional_sampler:
    window_seconds: 60
    alpha: 0.7
    beta: 0.3
    min_probability: 0.01
    max_probability: 0.5
    priority_scores:
      enterprise: 10
      standard: 1
      free: 0.2
    error_override: true
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [proportional_sampler]
      exporters: [redwood-exporter]
```

ana: love the explicit priority_scores. Also add a field to tag sampled traces with sampling_reason and sampling_budget_id so downstream exporters and the console can show why a trace was kept.

maya: good call. we should also emit metrics: sampled_by_route{route="/v1/generate",tier="enterprise"} and budget_exhausted{route=..}. console dashboard needs a stacked view of sampled vs dropped by route and by tier.

sophie: UX/rollout ask — would like a canary toggle per-route in the console (0-100% via slider) mapped to an override to sampling probability. Also audit logs for when someone bumps enterprise budgets.

raj: performance: when we do tail-sampling overrides, we need to avoid double-exporting the same trace. Suggest marker span attribute "redwood.sampling.finalized=true" and dedupe in exporter by trace_id with short TTL (e.g., 5m).

liam: how do we handle exporters/retention? if we aggressively drop spans at collector, we lose ability to reconstruct traces for post-mortem. Maybe keep a small prefix for all traces (span headers) and mark body as dropped. That way we can display partial traces.

maya: agree — plan: keep head spans (first 3 spans) for every trace at min. Tag them with "span.partial=true" if the rest was dropped. And keep full traces when sampled or error_override triggers.

telemetry-bot: note — this approach affects storage billing. ops will need per-tenant preserved_span_quota config + alerts when approaching limit.

sophie: for rollout: propose phases — (1) opt-in for internal teams (2) 10% public routes with budget cap (3) per-tenant bump via sales/CS request. We'll need an api: POST /admin/sampling/overrides {route,percent,expires,reason}.

maya: example override API payload:```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "percent": 20,
  "expires": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "reason": "canary for proportional sampler",
  "requested_by": "sophie"
}
```

raj: one more ops constraint — collector shards have memory spikes when many routes get ephemeral weights. Add a global cap on tracked routes and fall back to a default bucket.

liam: sounds good. next step: we should prototype the sampler in the collector with a stats exporter that feeds the console. I'll pick it up if maya posts a minimal PR.

maya: will do. I'll open a draft PR with the YAML and the sampling math plus unit tests. tagging @sophie for rollout plan and @raj for memory tests. :rocket:

deploy-bot: maya pushed branch proportional-sampler-proto. CI: queued.

sophie: thanks — can we also add a dashboard card that shows "expected token-saved" estimate when sampling rules change? product would like that to justify ops changes.
